items.difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the author theorem at source lines 567-570: there are second-order sentences with infinite models but no enumerable models. The author proof (572-584) exhibits the sentence negating the unit's Count sentence, which expresses enumerability of the domain in second-order logic, and observes that structures with nonenumerable domains, such as the power set of the naturals or the reals, satisfy it; the negated Count sentence then has infinite models, namely the nonenumerable ones, and no enumerable models. The strength of the example rests on the earlier established reading of Count, which the proof recalls and uses.
